Items.Authors: Elia Costa, Angelie Alagao, Alessandro Ballone, Andrea Baruffolo, Benedetta Di Francesco, Davide Greggio, Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Salvatore Lampitelli, Alessandro Lorenzetto, David Barr, Aurelie Magniez
Items.Title: EKARUS at Asiago Observatory: design and implementation of the instrument control software
Items.Abstract: The EKARUS project is a collaboration between LAM, ONERA, INAF, Durham University, and IPAG, aiming at bringing the Papyrus AO test bench at the 1.8m telescope of the Asiago Observatory. This paper details the design and implementation of the EKARUS Instrument Control Software (ICS), which is based on the PLICO Python framework. The architecture utilizes a distributed, service-oriented model, leveraging ZeroMQ (ZMQ) for communication between a central component “Sequencer like” and specialized hardware servers. A key design principle is strict hardware abstraction, this is a significant advantage for an R&D test bench as it guarantees high flexibility and rapid component upgrade cycles. The core work involves extending PLICO to integrate custom hardware. This modular architecture delivers strong adaptability and efficient support for the EKARUS AO bench infrastructure and its interface with the Real-Time Controller (RTC) and the Telescope Control System (TCS).

Items.Authors: Matteo Menessini, Lorenzo Busoni, Lorenzo Merli, Luca Cortese, Cedric Taissir Heritier, Davide Greggio, Carmelo Arcidiacono
Items.Title: EKARUS at the Asiago Observatory: simulations and performance analysis of a modular R&D ExAO system
Items.Abstract: EKARUS is a highly-modular R&D platform to be installed next year at Asiago, providing a SCAO correction with a first stage operating in the visible and with future upgrades for a second stage operating in the near IR and the inclusion of a pupil fragmentation unit to inject segment phasing errors. We performed simulations to determine the performance and the optimal AO parameters for different observing conditions. We started with an analytical error budget performed with TipTop, which was then validated with E2E simulations using SPECULA.  Simulation results are used to select the best options during the system's optical design and will provide key insights for optimization of the on-sky performance.

Items.Authors: Adam K. Taras, Barnaby Norris, Christopher Betters, Daniel Dahl, Nathan Long, Andrew Ross-Adams, Peter G. Tuthill, Jin Wei, Sergio Leon-Saval
Items.Title: Empirical spectro-polarimetric characterisation of photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns efficiently map input spatial modes to single-mode outputs for applications like high angular resolution imaging and nulling interferometry. However, manufacturing limits prevent full control over the device's mode transfer matrix at the design stage, making empirical characterization essential.   We present a system that directly measures the electric field of a photonic lantern's principal modes using digital off-axis holography over a 73nm range near 1550nm and in two orthogonal polarizations, unambiguously determining the device's transfer matrix. This is the first multi-wavelength, polarization-decomposed characterization.   Applying this to a 19-port lantern, we found significant differences from simulations in wavelength evolution rate and relative dispersion. Our results highlight the importance of measuring the as-fabricated device and we share the empirical transfer matrices to enable future astrophotonic design.

Items.Title: Engineering of titanium transition edge sensor wafers for the BA4 90/150 receiver of BICEP array
Items.Abstract: BA4-90/150, the fourth receiver in the BICEP Array series, is a dichroic 90/150 GHz instrument targeting the frequency space where sensitivity to the CMB polarization is maximized and is central to achieving σ(r) on the order of 0.001 with SPT delensing. Set for deployment in the 2026–2027 austral summer, it is projected to be the most sensitive receiver in the experiment deployed to date and introduces key innovations requiring tighter control of systematics, including optical and electrical crosstalk. Prototype titanium transition edge sensor wafers aim to reduce noise and inform the final integrated wafer for full receiver commissioning.

Items.Authors: Jayke S. Nguyen, Charlotte Guthery, Jacob Taylor, Mahawa Cisse, Antonin Bouchez, Jaren N. Ashcraft, Quinn Konopacky
Items.Title: Enhanced image sharpening for Keck AO using two-stage phase retrieval
Items.Abstract: Image sharpening corrects for the non-common path aberrations (NCPA) on adaptive optics systems and is an important step for adaptive optics calibration each night. The current image sharpening algorithm implemented on Keck uses focus diversity paired with a Gerchberg-Saxton phase retrieval algorithm. While the current workhorse algorithm works well, gradient-based phase retrieval methods have been shown to converge faster to a lower wavefront error. We present results from using a new and improved Python-based image sharpening code on the Keck AO bench. Furthermore, we analyze archival image sharpening data and find that most of the NCPA is in the form of an astigmatism on both Keck 1 and Keck 2. This likely originates from the IR dichroic on Keck 1 and Keck 2. Future plans include adding new image sharpening algorithms, such as nonlinear optimization techniques and using on-sky data to validate the relative improvement.

Items.Authors: Pierre Jouve, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel, Carlos Correia
Items.Title: Estimation of full-aperture uplink tip-tilt in laser guide star systems using spatial diversity and machine learning
Items.Abstract: Laser guide star adaptive optics systems greatly expand sky coverage for large telescopes but remain limited by their inability to sense uplink tip-tilt (TT), as no absolute reference exists at infinity. Low-order aberrations must therefore be obtained from natural guide stars (NGSs), constraining performance. Recent data-driven methods offer new ways to extract subtle information hidden in AO telemetry. We present a framework that exploits spatial diversity in a monostatic launch using a full-aperture 50-cm laser beam, combined with machine-learning inference, to estimate uplink TT directly from the LGS. The method reveals information previously inaccessible in LGS wavefront measurements. Under controlled conditions with a single layer and noiseless measurement, the model is able to retrieve 90% of the TT signal. With dual-layer turbulence with noisy measurements, it recovers up to 60% of the uplink signal. These results establish a clear proof of concept for uplink TT estimation.

Items.Authors: Max Braun, Scott C. Roberts, Peter Byrnes, John Rogers, Keivan Ahmadi, Joeleff Fitzsimmons
Items.Title: Evaluating the suitability of MEMS and piezoelectric accelerometers for structural vibration measurement in astronomical telescopes and instruments
Items.Abstract: We describe the development of an instrumented test-bed, including structure, optics and accelerometers, for experimental validation of integrated modeling results. We utilize integrated modeling tools to predict the optical response of the test-bed given a generated disturbance from a modal shaker. The integrated model uses the measured accelerations on the structure to predict the structural dynamics of the system and the resulting optical degradation. The actual optical degradation is measured with a wavefront sensor at the output of the optical system. While piezoelectric accelerometers are more sensitive, and have a lower noise floor, the cost advantage of MEMS-based accelerometers makes them attractive candidates. We present measurements of the performance of various accelerometers and estimate the error in measurement of each type against a typical vibration environment for our test-bed and for typical use cases on astronomical telescopes and instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Fabian Haberhauer, Oliver Czoske, Hugo Buddelmeijer, Kieran Leschinski, Janus Brink, Werner Zeilinger
Items.Title: Evolving ScopeSim: an integrated online exposure simulator for the ELT
Items.Abstract: The European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) demands modern, high-fidelity observation simulation tools capable of handling its complex optical and adaptive optics systems. ScopeSim, developed at the University of Vienna, already provides realistic simulations for several ELT instruments, but its current deployment is limited to local installations, and is mostly used by instrument consortium members. We present its expansion into a scalable, web-based service designed to support the broader ELT/VLT community. The platform will offer validated instrument packages, visualization tools, and consistent feedback mechanisms for astronomers, proposal reviewers, and observatory staff. This development addresses a critical gap in current observation-planning infrastructure and provides a flexible, future-proof solution for next-generation observatories.

Items.Authors: M. Rejkuba, N. Alas Silva, T. Bierwirth, H. M. J. Boffin, S. Brillant, O. R. Hainaut, M. Korpan, F. Patat, M. Prümm, M. F. Sterzik, A. Weiss, M. Wittkowski
Items.Title: Evolving time allocation and scheduling for the ESO VLT and VLTI
Items.Abstract: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) has transitioned its main Call for Proposals from a 6-monthly to a yearly cadence. To complement this change, ESO is introducing a new Fast Track Channel, designed to support observing proposals motivated by emerging scientific opportunities that require a response on a timescale of a few months. These changes necessitated substantial updates to ESO’s time allocation and scheduling processes, as well as the underlying software tools. We present the evolution of ESO’s scheduling framework that simultaneously accommodates scientific observations and technical time requests. The system incorporates novel concepts for managing commitments across overlapping cycles and accounting for the remaining science fraction from previously accepted proposals. New science proposals and new or updated technical time requests are scheduled within the same optimisation environment. The scheduler includes the joint optimisation of multiple telescope schedules.

Items.Authors: Dohoon Kim, Il kweon Moon, Hyukson Kwon, Gisung Park, Yunjong Kim, Jongwan Ko, Jihun Kim, JaeYeong Jo, Taejong Kim, Minho Seo, Yeonsik Kim, Sang Hun Lee, Seunghyik Chang
Items.Title: Fabrication and metrology of off-axis freeform mirrors for the K-DRIFT G1 telescope
Items.Abstract: We fabricated and tested three freeform mirrors for the KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope, a confocal off-axis three-mirror system with a 300 mm entrance pupil diameter. To reduce weight, lightweighting design was applied to the primary and tertiary mirrors, resulting in weight reductions of 73.2 % and 73.9 %, respectively. The secondary mirror (SM) was not subject to the lightweighting process. Surface profiles were measured using Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMMs) during grinding. For polishing and finishing, CGH was used for the primary and tertiary mirrors (PM, TM), while LuphoScan was used for the secondary mirror (SM). All mirrors met the required surface accuracy of 20 nm RMS and 100 nm PV.

Items.Authors: David J. Thoen, Dimitry Lamers, Martijn Veen, Daniela Perez Capelo, Marcel P. Bruijn, Tonny H. M. Coppens, Arno Gotink, Ton J. van der Linden, Kenichiro Nagayoshi, Vishal Anvekar, Rene A. van der Windt, Paolo M. Sberna, Shahab O. Dabironezare, Jochem J. A. Baselmans
Items.Title: Fabrication development for the lens-antenna coupled and lens-absorber coupled kinetic inductance detector arrays for PRIMAger
Items.Abstract: PRIMA is a next generation far-infrared space telescope, with cryogenically cooled optics, coupling to ultrasensitive lens-coupled microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID) arrays. In this paper we explain the detailed fabrication procedure of the lens-antenna and lens-absorber coupled detectors for the PRIMA Polarimetric Imager (PPI) and PRIMA Hyperspectral Imager (PHI), respectively. Emphasis will be placed on the aluminium preparation, patterning and its step coverage. We elaborate on how we make the fabrication reliable and exactly to specification with thousands of membranes and detectors on a single 100 mm diameter wafer.

Items.Authors: Ceiwynn C. Longworth, Megan M. Delamer, Suvrath Mahadevan, Joe P. Ninan, Kathleen Gehoski, Krushna Jadhav
Items.Title: Fabrication of focusing optics for TA-MOONS: Micro-MOONS
Items.Abstract: Tackling open problems in star formation requires precise spectroscopic observations of a large number of young stellar objects, spanning a wide wavelength band from the optical through the near-infrared. The TIFR-ARIES Multi-Object Optical to Near-infrared Spectrometer (TA-MOONS) is a new astronomical instrument designed to survey young stars. To precisely position starlight into its 8 robotic arms, an array of microscopic, concave mirrors is needed. The fabrication of the mirror array called Micro-MOONS was done using two-photon polymerization 3D printing. The mirrors are created of IP-S photoresist on a silicon substrate, with fabrication focusing on uniformity, minimizing surface roughness, and preserving the desired curvature radius.

Items.Authors: Kosuke Kushibiki, Kentaro Motohara, Tadayuki Kodama, Masayuki Akiyama, Yosuke Minowa, Yusei Koyama, Ichi Tanaka, Kumiko Morihana, Kenshi Yanagisawa, Sadman Ali, Takashi Hattori, Michitoshi Yoshida, Masahiro Konishi, Shiang-Yu Wang
Items.Title: Final design of wide field imager (WFI) for ULTIMATE-Subaru
Items.Abstract: Wide Field Imager (WFI) is a near-infrared (0.9–2.5 μm) imager which covers a wide field of view and samples high-spatial resolution realized by a new Ground Layer Adaptive Optics system of the Subaru Telescope, called ULTIMATE-Subaru, delivering 0.2" image quality in the K-band over a 20' field of view (FoV).     To cover its wide FoV, WFI consists of four identical optical units, each covering a 6.7′ x 6.7′ FoV, for a total FoV of 14.4′ x 14.4′. Each unit accommodates up to 20 filters, including broad-, medium-, and narrow-band filters, and to operate a larger number of filters, narrow-band filters are designed to be easily exchangeable. A HAWAII-4RG detector with 0.1″/pixel sampling is used per unit.     The final design of WFI is almost completed, and production will commence soon. In this presentation, we will describe the WFI’s specifications, technical details, and current development status.

Items.Authors: Mala Mateen, Kyler R. Langworthy, James Mathis, Jackson Stearns, William Gibson, Tanya Tavenner, Scott Newey, Mark Eickhoff, Odell Reynolds, Ian Kingsolver, Robert Johnson, Patrick Kelly
Items.Title: First light results from Castor AO
Items.Abstract: An adaptive optics (AO) system was developed for the 1.0-meter Castor, ground-based, optical telescope. The system is operated by the Starfire Optical Range in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The system saw first light on 29 Jun 2025 and achieved diffraction limited imaging in I- and J-band. The adaptive optics system is located at coudé focus, and it features a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor that can operate in two optical configurations: 10×10 and 6×6 subapertures. The 10×10 configuration allows the correction of a higher number of modes, relative to the 6×6 configuration, which is optimized for dim objects detection. Wavefront sensing is performed at visible wavelengths, while tilt-control and AO-corrected imagery is made in the near-infrared. This paper describes the first AO observations, and presents the photometric measurements for the imaging paths, including AO performance vs. limiting magnitude.

Items.Authors: Benjamin J. Weiner, Grant Williams, Timothy Pickering, J. Duane Gibson, Dallan Porter, Sean Moran
Items.Title: Flexible scheduling and queue observing with Binospec and MMIRS at the MMT Observatory
Items.Abstract: Binospec and MMIRS are optical and IR wide-field spectrographs operated in queue mode at the MMT Observatory in Arizona, currently queue scheduled for 100-120 nights/semester. PIs design observations, slitmasks, and upload targets for Binospec and MMIRS through web interfaces run by MMT and SAO. At night, a scheduling program ranks observing blocks, from which the queue observers choose targets appropriate to conditions. Pipelines run by SAO scientists return reduced data to the PIs through the web interface. MMT instrument scientists support both the PIs and QOs as intermediaries. Queue observing has many advantages for flexibility, especially for time domain astronomy and targets of opportunity. However, it separates the PIs from the observing process, adding pressure on observation design to communicate the science goals, and on the observatory to manage PI expectations. We will discuss the Observatory Manager web interfaces and some of the common pinch points in queue operations.

Items.Authors: Michael Jones, Christopher B. Mendillo, Caroline Desgranges
Items.Title: Focal plane wavefront correction for dark hole creation with a neural network on PICTURE-D
Items.Abstract: In order to directly image exoplanets, a dark hole is created in the coronagraph science camera image, which is a region where light speckles are minimized to improve the contrast ratio. Creation of a dark hole normally consists of two independent steps: sensing and correction. During sensing, the electric field (EF) in the focal plane is determined, then during correction, a command is applied to the deformable mirror(s) to minimize the EF. The PICTURE-D balloon mission makes use of the linear EF Conjugation (EFC) algorithm for EF correction. However, this algorithm has two limitations: first, the corrections require a nonlinear model, whereas EFC relies on an inverted matrix, and second, EFC may not properly describe the optical system. Therefore, a neural network (NN) is developed for EF correction on PICTURE-D and will target the issue of nonlinearity. It is shown, in simulation, that a NN can obtain a higher contrast ratio after one iteration when compared with EFC.

Items.Authors: Georgios N. Vassilakis, Susan F. Redmond, Jason D. Rhodes, Richard J. Massey, Qiuhan He
Items.Title: Forecasting PSF stability requirements for low-mass dark matter subhalo detection with the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: Current optical and near-infrared strong-lensing detections of dark matter subhalos remain concentrated at ≥10^8 M_sun. HWO may probe the 10^6–10^8 M_sun regime, but these detections require PSF models accurate enough that optical residuals do not erase or mimic subhalo signals. We present HWO-SLAPS (HWO Strong Lensing Analysis Pipeline for Subhalos), a simulation and inference pipeline that generates galaxy-galaxy lenses with embedded dark matter subhalos, convolves them with concept HWO-like segmented-mirror PSF models spanning several aberration modes, and adds observational and detector noise. We then combine Fisher/Asimov forecasts, PyAutoLens nonlinear searches, and Bayesian evidence comparisons to quantify detectability versus mass and PSF modeling accuracy. In a single canonical lensing scene, PSF-bank-marginalized evidence recovers most 1.0×10^7 M_sun subhalos and reaches near-complete recovery at 1.0×10^7.25 M_sun, while PSF mismatch can produce false subhalo evidence.

Items.Authors: Hans J. Kärcher, Harald E. Nicklas
Items.Title: Four decades of technical progress in building Large Optical Telescopes
Items.Abstract: Now, with ongoing assembly of the European Extremely Large Telescope ESO/ELT and its commissioning at the end of this decade, and the manufacturing of the Giant Magellan Telescope GMT on the way, the era of the Very Large Telescopes is on its summit. Forty years ago, the progress in sensor technology and digital control initiated, that astronomers’ dreams of building telescopes beyond the 4-Meter-Class became reasonable. Active optics allowed the construction of large monolithic and segmented mirrors and initiated the worldwide planning and realization of very large telescope projects. The paper presents a comparison of the different design approaches of that time: an overview on their optical arrangements, the available mirror technologies and mechanical mounting concepts, including structural layout, axis mechanisms and related performance control strategies. The paper aims for an assessment of the technical progress from an engineer’s point of view that has been achieved over last f

Items.Authors: Marco Colussi, Leo Colussi, Marco Mattietto, Gianmarco Franceschini, Andrea Fadalti, Nicola Casoni, Niccolò De Bona, Daniele Nieddu, Pascal Martinez, Mark Wallace
Items.Title: From final design to first alignment: advancements in the ELT Main Structure
Items.Abstract: The ELT Main Structure (MS), an alt-azimuth system weighing about 4500 t, is now undergoing advanced construction and early commissioning at Cerro Armazones. It mainly consists of a steel space-frame structure highly optimized to guarantee high dynamic stiffness, tight pointing performance, and controlled deformation. A dedicated 3D seismic isolation system ensures resistance under extreme site conditions. The paper outlines the final MS design and summarizes progress in manufacturing, erection, structural interfaces and initial alignment verification.

Items.Authors: Béatrice Lessard-Hamel, Rajbir Singh, Denis Brousseau, Frédéric Lamontagne, Hugues Auger, Simon Thibault
Items.Title: From manufacturing to optical performance: validation of the GIRMOS image slicer assembly
Items.Abstract: Image slicers (SLI) are now standard components in astronomical instrumentation, particularly for Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS). Our team at the Advanced Optical Fabrication Infrastructure (AOFI) has been tasked with the fabrication of the slicer-based IFU for GIRMOS (Gemini InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph), which consists of 42 270-um width slices with their corresponding pupil and field mirrors, for a total of 126 optical surfaces. We have manufactured one full slicer assembly within the required tight optical tolerances. Here we present our metrology, and tests procedures, including optical testing based on optical simulations. A comprehensive metrology and assembly workflow was implemented using a ZYGO NewviewTM NX2 optical profiler and a VIS slicer test bench developed based on a room-temperature optical model. Together, these metrology steps demonstrate that the slicer assembly meets the required optical performance at warm conditions.

Items.Authors: Jose Antonio Quero, Elena Colomo, Guillermo Buendía
Items.Title: From submission to operations: a proposal handling system for scientific missions
Items.Abstract: From the opening of a Call for Proposals until the scientific proposals are finally ingested into a mission's operational environment, several months elapse. During this time, the proposal passes through various subsystems and phases: submission, approval, optimization, and finally ingestion. Integrating all of this presents significant challenges.    The goal for missions like XMM-Newton or XRISM, which handle numerous Guest Observer proposals, is to create a common framework, from the first PI’s initial request until the proposal has been approved and even observed. To achieve this, we are working on modern software that takes this traceability into account (XIPS for proposal submission, XPET for proposal evaluation), and we are developing new projects to close the entire cycle.    Additionally, we are developing new end-to-end environments in Kubernetes to validate complete integration across the entire Proposal Handling System.

Items.Authors: Qianhan Zhou, Lanqiang Zhang, Nanfei Yan, Jianhui Zhang, Xin Liu, Yongxin Zeng, Jinsheng Yang, Xuejun Rao, Changhui Rao
Items.Title: Global wavefront reconstruction strategy for dual-WFS multiconjugate adaptive optics system
Items.Abstract: We propose a global wavefront reconstruction strategy for dual-sensor multi-conjugate adaptive optics (MCAO) systems, addressing the suboptimal performance and numerical instability of conventional reconstructors. From a control perspective, our method integrates the optical layout of dual wavefront sensors to enable stable estimation of ground-layer and high-altitude aberrations. Implemented on an MCAO experimental platform with layered turbulence and multiple guide stars, the approach outperforms conventional single-sensor and sequential decoupled schemes. Closed-loop experiments show that under r0=15cm, the proposed global GLAO+HAC reconstruction achieves a field-averaged Strehl ratio of 21.93%, with reduced coefficient of variation indicating improved field uniformity.

Items.Authors: Nerea Castro, Armando Bilbao, Alberto Fernández, Paula Sierra, Bruce Bigelow, Eduardo Villar, Christopher Madden, Miroslav Vulinovic, Francisco Meza, Hector Swett, Ángel Gomez, Lourdes Cabezuelo, Esther Fernández, Juan Martinez, Francisco José Sanchez, Miguel Martin, Arantza De Echenique, Rodrigo Pereira, Gustavo Arriagada
Items.Title: GMT site, enclosure, and facilities: facing the construction phase
Items.Abstract: In July 2024, the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) enclosure design successfully passed its Final Design Review, achieving the “Ready for Construction” milestone and consolidating two years of detailed engineering. This phase prioritized a cost-effective and reliable solution, optimized for efficient construction at the remote Las Campanas site. The design integrates a wide range of disciplines—including structural (concrete and steel), mechanisms, MEP systems, telescope-specific utilities, control systems, telescope seismic isolation system and architectural elements—ensuring compliance with the observatory´s stringent technical and operational requirements.  Following this milestone, GMTO and IDOM have continued their collaboration to further enhance the enclosure´s performance, refine construction documentation and advance the development of additional summit facilities and infrastructure. Bi-parting shutter’s latching system, Summit Support Building are some of these examples.

Items.Authors: Marianne Cox, Sam Chan, Jorge Barrios, Rafael Ovando, José M. Filgueira, Efren Sandoval, Arushan Badasyan
Items.Title: GMTO cybersecurity strategies and integration with the GMT Observatory control system
Items.Abstract: Large research institutions, such as observatories, face unique challenges in cybersecurity and are becoming more frequent targets of cyberattacks. It is critical that cybersecurity strategies are built into the design from the very beginning, and control measures are put in place to prevent vulnerabilities from arising as the observatory infrastructure evolves. GMTO is an active member and contributor of the Trusted CI Framework, a standard for cybersecurity programs tailored for research infrastructure, and have developed a Cybersecurity Program Strategic Plan (CPSP) to guide future updates. The Observatory Control System sits behind the cybersecurity-layer provided by the IT infrastructure, but requires secure access control for remote operations, interfaces with third-party services, and data life-cycle management. In this paper we describe the current GMTO cybersecurity implementation, and strategies for the integration with the Observatory Control System (OCS).

Items.Authors: Saavidra Perera, Vincent Chambouleyron, Jérôme Maire, Clarissa R. Do Ó, Jayke S. Nguyen, Quinn M. Konopacky, Jeffrey Chilcote, Brian Sands, Randall Hamper, Matthew Engstrom, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Dan Kerley, Bruce Macintosh, Christian Marois, Fredrik Rantakyrö, Dmitry Savransky, Jean-Pierre Véran, Guido Agapito, S. Mark Ammons, Marco Bonaglia, Marc-André Boucher, Joel Burke, Ed Chapin, Daren Dilon, Jennifer Dunn, Simone Esposito, Guillaume Filion, Öykü Galvan, Jean Thomas Landry, Olivier Lardière, Duan Li, Alex Madurowicz, Teo Mocnik, Dillon Peng, Lisa Poyneer, Carlos Quiroz, Garima Singh, Eckhart Spalding, Nicole Wolff
Items.Title: GPI 2.0: calibration of the pyramid wavefront sensor
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Planet Imager (GPI) is a high-contrast imaging instrument designed to directly detect and characterise young, Jupiter-mass exoplanets. After six years of operation at Gemini South in Chile, the instrument is being upgraded and moved to Gemini North in Hawaii as GPI 2.0. Several improvements have been made to the adaptive optics system as part of this upgrade. This includes replacing the current Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor with a pyramid wavefront sensor (PWFS) with a custom EMCCD, and employing the Herzberg Extensible Adaptive Real-Time Toolkit (HEART). These changes will increase GPI’s sky coverage by accessing fainter targets, improving corrections on fainter stars, and enabling faster and ultra-low-latency operations on brighter targets. The PWFS subsystem was independently built and tested to verify its performance before being integrated into the GPI 2.0 instrument. In this paper, we will present GPI 2.0 AO pre-shipping performance and calibration test results.

Items.Authors: Nicole Wolff, Jayke S. Nguyen, Bruce Macintosh, Saavidra Perera, Emiel Por, Vincent Chambouleyron, Jérôme Maire, Clarissa R. Do Ó, Quinn M. Konopacky, Jeffrey Chilcote, Brian Sands, Matthew Engstrom, Randall Hamper, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Dan Kerley, Christian Marois, Fredrik Rantakyrö, Dmitry Savransky, Jean-Pierre Veran, Guido Agapito, S. Mark Ammons, Marco Bonaglia, Marc-Andre Boucher, Joel Burke, Daren Dillon, Jennifer Dunn, Simone Esposito, Guillaume Filion, Oyku Galvan, Gwyneth Lannon, Jean Thomas Landry, Olivier Lardiere, Duan Li, Alex Madurowicz, Dillon Peng, Lisa Poyneer, Garima Singh, Eckhart Spalding
Items.Title: GPI 2.0: Simulated Performance of the AO Upgrade
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Planet Imager Upgrade (GPI 2.0) is undergoing final testing before it is integrated into the Gemini North Telescope on Mauna Kea. The upgrade includes a pyramid wavefront sensor and advanced apodized-pupil Lyot coronagraph masks designed to block both telescope structures and bad DM actuators. In preparation for instrument commissioning and first light science, we present results of end-to-end simulations of the GPI 2.0 adaptive optics (AO) system and coronagraph that span AO control parameters (pyramid modulation, loop frequency, loop gain) and observing parameters (stellar magnitude, exposure time, seeing). As part of this, we investigate the tolerance to coronagraphic misalignments and non-common path errors under atmospheric conditions realistic to Mauna Kea. Finally, we present a performance comparison between measured raw contrasts of the original GPI survey and simulations of the GPI 2.0 upgrade.

Items.Authors: Miska Le Louarn, Pierre-Yves Madec
Items.Title: Ground layer adaptive optics for 8-12m telescopes
Items.Abstract: In this contribution, we will outline the simulations made for a 12m wide field telescope, using ground layer adaptive optics (GLAO), on a 3-6' corrected field, in the visible.   We will present performance estimates using different methods, for a GLAO system using 3 natural guide stars.   First, simply filtering different amounts of layers in the Cn2 profile. Then, we will use a Fourier tool to present statistical information on the image quality improvements grought by GLAO. Finally, we will use a few End to End simulations to validate our findings.  We will show the distribution of image quality over a large number of measured Cn2 profiles, obtained by using a SCIDAR.  We also propose other concepts, like Rayleigh laser guide stars, and discuss the pros and cons of NGS and LGS in this context.

Items.Authors: Kuo-Chia (Alice) Liu, Jeffrey Smith, Marie Levine, Charley Noecker, Joshua Abel, James Govern, Jon Lawrence, Jordan Effron, Gregory Walsh, Kenneth Dziak, Joseph Howard, Alan Gostin, Cameron Haag, Gary Kuan, Connor Mulrenin, Breann Sitarski, John Ziemer
Items.Title: Habitable Worlds Observatory: exploratory analytic cases formulation and analysis
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is a NASA flagship space telescope designed to identify and characterize habitable zone exoplanets and advance our understanding of the universe through general astrophysics observations. Currently in pre-formulation, the project has defined Exploratory Analytic Cases (EACs) to address demanding science objectives while exploring challenging engineering parameters through architecture and trade space studies. This paper describes the first three EACs and their lessons learned, discusses the integrated modeling pipeline, and shares key trade study results. These findings have guided EACs 4 and 5, which will further explore the trade space and prepare for the baseline design supporting the Mission Concept Review.

Items.Authors: Jean-Emmanuel Migniau, Alexandre Jeanneau, Matthieu Guibert, Magali Loupias, Loïs Duran, Alban Remillieux, Victor Mauger-Vauglin, Eric Daguisé, Rémi Giroud, Nicolas Bouché, Pascal Huguet-Chantome, Didier Rousse
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: cryogenic mirror mount based on bonded Invar supports
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025. The Integral Field Unit (IFU) sub-system is part of an Integral Field Spectrograph cooled down to 130K. The IFU is in charge of splitting, slicing and rearranging the rectangular field of view into 4 long slits (~540mm) to feed 4 spectrographs. For encumbrance reasons, some mirror have been glued onto their invar support. This paper presents the design of one glued mirror case, the simulation of its thermal behaviour and the result obtained during testing a prototype inside a test cryostat. The conclusion summarises the foreseen results for the full IFU.

Items.Authors: Guillermo Mercant Rubio, Iago Funes Vecino, Alonso Álvarez Urueña, Laura García Moreno, Gonzalo José Carracedo Carballal, Irene Ferro Rodríguez, Heribert Argelaguet Vilaseca, Chiara Cerruti, Javier Piqueras López
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: design & tests on the current status of low order wavefront subsystem pick off arm engineering model (LPOA-EM)
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first-light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. Following a 2025 rescope phase, the project is resuming its final design. This review significantly impacted the Low Order Wavefront Subsystem (LOWFS) and its LPOU/LPOA unit, requiring the simultaneous operation of three LPOAs. This work details the opto-mechanical layout, electronic implementation, and planned tests for the LPOA Engineering Model (EM), adapted for HARMONI operation under MORFEO.

Items.Authors: Kieran McCall, Edgar Castillo Domínguez, Liam Boland, Matthias Tecza, Miriam Estefania Cisneros González, Eduard Muslimov, Eleni Sarakinou, James Kariuki, Sophie Paszynska, Angela Mills, Niranjan Thatte
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: evaluation of opto-mechanical bonding: adhesive performance, substrate compatibility, and transportation viability
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics-assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025. This paper presents an evaluation of Opto-mechanical bonding for the ISP by investigating various adhesives and substrates. It assesses their viability, performance, and manufacturability. The bonding is crucial in four main interfaces of glass to metal in the ISP:   1.Bulky, long and static collimator mirrors  2.Bulky and heavy static lenses in the infrared camera  3.Flat composite movable gratings in the Infared Grating Module (IGM)   4.Flat light movable mirrors for the Folding Mirror Mechanism (FMM)     All the information will be used in the updated design of the ISP.

Items.Authors: Gonzalo José Carracedo Carballal, Irene M. Ferro Rodríguez, David King, Iago Funes Vecino, Guillermo Mercant Rubio, Heribert Argelaguet Vilaseca, Alonso Álvarez Urueña, Laura García Moreno, Javier Piqueras López, Chiara Cerruti
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: LPOU calibrations for a micron-level pointing accuracy
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800 nm to 2450 nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25 mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025.    In previous designs, the geometrical calibration reference for the guiding probes took the form of a deployable calibration mask that could be inserted in the telescope's focal plane. In this work we explore the possibility of inserting the calibration mask closer the guiding probes, effectively decoupling optical and mechanical effects during the calibration process. The results of these analyses were performed and validated by means of optical simulations in RayZaler, and will be used to put bounds to the expected calibration accuracy achievable by this design.

Items.Authors: Miriam E. Cisneros-González, James Kariuki, Liam Boland, Edgar Castillo-Domínguez, Kieran McCall, Eduard R. Muslimov, Sophie Paszynska, Matthias Tecza
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: repeatability analysis of the spectrograph dispersers wheel mechanism
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-infrared integral field spectrograph for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The University of Oxford is in charge of the design and development of the four identical spectrographs that constitute the ISP subsystem. During the past few months, the spectrographs design has been substantially optimized to reduce the number of mechanisms exposed to cryogenic conditions. The updated version of the dispersers wheel module is a reduced size of the original Infrared Grating Wheel (IGW) presented in previous works. This work presents the different repeatability tests performed in the prototype mechanism, and the achieved stability results, including operation at room conditions, warm temperature in vacuum conditions, and cryogenic conditions.

Items.Authors: A. J. Eldorado Riggs, Garreth Ruane, Jorge Llop-Sayson, John J. Gill, Sofia Rahiminejad, Daniel W. Wilson, Camilo Prada, Emory L. Jenkins, Ramya Anche, Corey Fucetola, Ewan S. Douglas
Items.Title: High contrast testbed results with black silicon shaped pupils
Items.Abstract: NASA plans to image terrestrial exoplanets with the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). HWO's large primary mirror will most likely be segmented, which introduces extra diffraction in the image. Apodization, either with deformable mirrors or a dedicated mask, is needed to suppress this diffraction. Reflective apodizers for the Roman Coronagraph were flight qualified and demonstrated 4e-9 contrast in vacuum testbeds. In our current work, we aim to show that black silicon apodizers can provide the 1e-10 contrast needed by HWO. Last year for our first milestone, we showed that the incoherent light contribution from scattering off black silicon is negligible for the HWO contrast budget. Our next milestone is to achieve <5e-10 raw contrast on the Decadal Survey Testbed 2 bench in vacuum with a shaped pupil coronagraph. Here we present our most recent testbed results.

Items.Authors: Dijana Bogunovic, Bernard Delabre, Tony Reed, Graeme Jonas, Andrew Rakich, George Maddever, Gergely Hajdu, Rolf Chini, Mikolaj Kaluszynski, Marek Gorski, Mirek Kicia, Grzegorz Pietrzynski
Items.Title: High resolution spectrograph for the Nicolaus Copernicus Astronomical Center (CAMK)
Items.Abstract: KiwiStar Optics/EOS Optical Technologies is contracted to build a high-resolution, high radial velocity (RV) precision spectrograph for the Nicolaus Copernicus Astronomical Center’s (CAMK) Rolf Chini Cerro Murphy Observatory (OCM) at Cerro Murphy, next to the ESO-ELT in the Chilean Atacama Desert. The instrument is scheduled to be installed at the end of 2027. It will be fiber-fed from a Nasmyth port of the F/7 Ritchey-Chrétien 2.5 m telescope currently being built by Astro Systeme Austria (ASA).  KiwiStar’s highly versatile KiwiSpec echelle R4-100, bench mounted spectrograph design, successfully implemented in the MAROON-X and MINERVA North/South spectrographs, is upgraded to improve the stability and throughput of the system while keeping the same small footprint of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Damien Prêle, Sotiris Loucatos, Manuel Gonzalez, Jean-Luc Sauvageot, Xavier de la Broïse, Jean-Batiste Melin, Ahmad Itawi, Timothée Tollet, Gwendal Deniel
Items.Title: High-density superconducting flex cables for cryogenic TES and SQUID interconnections
Items.Abstract: We report the development of high-density superconducting flexible cables for TES/SQUID interconnections. Nb or Nb/Ti thin films on polyimide enable low-loss biasing and readout with extremely low parasitic resistance at cryogenic temperatures.  Over two years, a collaboration involving APC/CNRS, CEA/Irfu, SLAC, CERN, and industry (Hightec, Cicor) has focused on a reproducible process meeting strict requirements on Tc, Ic, and residual resistance.  The initial CERN pilot production provided an additional process validation step and feedback on patterning, bonding, and cleanliness, complementing earlier Hightec and Cicor runs that already demonstrated satisfactory superconducting performance. Subsequent iterations show improved process understanding and increased process stability across technologies.

Items.Authors: Ben Sappey, Ashely D. Baker, Jérôme Maire, Andrea S. J. Lin, Quinn M. Konopacky, Nemanja Jovanovic, Samuel P. Halverson, Dimitri Mawet, Michael Fitzgerald, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, Bryson Cale, Rose Gibson, Stephanie Leifer, Jocelyn Ferrara, Rob Bertz
Items.Title: HISPEC calibration unit update: integration, testing, and performance
Items.Abstract: We present an update on the HISPEC Calibration Unit (CAL), a multi-source system enabling precision radial velocities, Doppler imaging, and high-contrast high-resolution spectroscopy of nearby exoplanets. CAL combines two astro-etalons, two laser frequency combs, a U/Ne/Ar hollow cathode lamp (HCL), and a suite of gas absorption cells, all delivered via single-mode fibers for use during science observations or daytime calibrations. We have completed construction of the subsystem and begun integration and testing. The y/J-band and H/K-band astro-etalons show long-term linear drift rates of 24.5 and 7.2 cm/s/day, respectively, with residual drifts of $\pm 1-2$m/s correlated with ambient temperature. The gas cells, as observed by PARVI, achieve median per-order RV calibration uncertainties of 4.6 m/s in J-band and 3.5 m/s in H-band. The uranium HCL delivers 1.3 m/s (median) in J-band, and we see emission features from U, Ne, and Ar, suggesting both fill gasses are used in manufacturing.

Items.Authors: Olga Zamora, José Acosta, José Peñate, Teodora Viera, Marta Aguiar, Rosa Clavero, Joan Caseras
Items.Title: IAC80Pol: polarimetry with small diameter telescopes
Items.Abstract: IAC80Pol is a new dual-beam polarimetric capability proposed for the IAC80 telescope to enable high-cadence photopolarimetric follow-up of bright and moderately faint variable sources. Motivated by the growing demand for rapid characterization of transient events, the instrument combines a calcite analyzer and a rotating half-wave plate to measure linear polarization with low instrumental contamination. Simulations show that polarization uncertainties below 0.3% are achievable for sources around R≈17 with short exposure times. The design leverages previous successful implementations on similar small-aperture telescopes and aims to support studies of blazars, supernovae, GRBs, and other transient phenomena. Future extensions may include polarization mapping of extended sources and interstellar dust.

Items.Authors: Davide Mollica, Ciro Bigongiari, Antonino D'Aì, Fabio Pintore, Saverio Lombardi
Items.Title: iactsim: a GPU-accelerated IACT simulation framework
Items.Abstract: Performance evaluation and data analysis of next-generation Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) depend on large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. Although extensive air shower simulation is the main bottleneck, telescope response simulation can become quite time-consuming during the design and commissioning phases. To address this, we been developing iactsim, a GPU-accelerated Python simulation framework for IACTs. In this work, we demonstrate the framework capabilities simulating the telescope for the ASTRI mini-array project, ray-tracing the entire Schwarzschild-Couder optical system, and simulating the response of the ASTRI Silicon Photomultiplier Cherenkov camera. We present validation results comparing simulated data with data from the first two operational ASTRI Mini-Array telescopes and report preliminary benchmarks indicating a speedup of two orders of magnitude compared over the current CPU-based ASTRI simulator.

Items.Authors: Ilaria Ermolli, Roberto Cirami, Kamal Sant, Dario Del Moro, Paolo Romano, Bernard Gelly, Richard Douet, Giorgio Viavattene, Veronica Baldini, Fabrizio Giorgi, Mariarita Murabito, Luca Oggioni, Giovanna Jerse, Fabiana Ferrente, Lidia Contarino, Teodora Mihailescu, Antonio Sulich, Igor Coretti, Maurizio Oliviero, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Giorgio Calderone, Salvatore Luigi Guglielmino, Matteo Aliverti, Luca Giovannelli, Mauro Centrone, Etienne Pariat, Giorgio Frazzoni, Valentina Alberti, Roberto Piazzesi, Fernando Pedichini, Sara Bertocco, Edoardo Redaelli
Items.Title: IBIS 2.0: interferometric bidimensional spectrometer 2.0 at the THEMIS solar telescope
Items.Abstract: The IBIS2.0 project aims to upgrade the Interferometric BIdimensional Spectrometer, originally operated at the Dunn Solar Telescope of the National Solar Observatory from 2003 to 2019, for its relocation and installation at the THEMIS solar telescope at the Teide Observatory. The refurbished instrument integrates the original dual Fabry-Perrot etalons with a new polarimetric unit, interference filters, new scientific cameras, and a fully modernised instrument control and data-handling system. These upgrades to the scientific sensors and the control system have enabled us to automate the instrument's operations. IBIS2.0 is designed to preserve the spectral coverage of the original system (580-860 nm) while offering enhanced stability and robustness.   The integration (Hardware and Software) of the instrument at THEMIS is currently underway. In this contribution, we present the installation progress at the new telescope as well as the new observational capabilities that it will offer.

Items.Authors: Michael P. Smith, Elliott Horch, Marsha Wolf, George Ayer, Matthew Buchkowski, Nicholas Devries, Sebastian Lucero, Kathleen Jurgella, Jacob Mader, Max Martone, Jessica McKeon, Fiona Powers Ozyurt, Ana Baculima, Macy Dennon, Christine Broadbridge
Items.Title: IFUSI: the integral field unit speckle imager
Items.Abstract: We will present the progress of IFUSI, the Integral Field Unit Speckle Imager. This instrument, planned for the 4.3-m Lowell Discovery Telescope, will use a ~2100-fiber integral field unit to record spectra over a highly-magnified ~1.1 arcsec field of view. From these spectra, it will be possible to reconstruct speckle patterns which are then analyzed to produce diffraction-limited images. The instrument comprises a magnifier module, IFU, and four spectrographs. The magnifier module will provide a magnification of 60x to ensure that speckles are critically sampled. From the focal plane, the beam passes through two dichroic beamsplitters, which limit the wavelength range transmitted to the IFU. Additionally, the light reflected from the beamsplitters is also reimaged onto two EMCCD detectors, allowing for two “normal” speckle imaging channels. The IFU and fiber cable feed four modest-sized spectrographs designed to use COTS components, with the spectral images captured on four EMCCDs.

Items.Authors: Yusufjon A. Tillayev, Azimjon Azimov, Miska Le Louarn, Aktam Hafizov, Shuhrat Ehgamberdiev
Items.Title: Impact of meteorological parameters to the observatory operation
Items.Abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of meteorological parameters measured at the Maidanak Astronomical  Observatory over the period 2012–2025, aimed at characterizing the site for the planned installation of a new 4 m  telescope. The study includes annual and monthly statistics of key variables such as wind speed and direction, air  temperature, and relative humidity, with more than 400,000 nighttime measurements analyzed for each parameter.  Long-term temperature trends are investigated, including a comparison with earlier (1996–2002) data to assess  potential signals of regional climate change. The results provide critical information on site stability and  atmospheric conditions, supporting both engineering specifications and long-term operational planning for future  astronomical observations.

Items.Authors: Marcio Melendez, Laurent Pueyo, Nicolas Flagey, Randal Telfer, Matt Lallo, Jon Arenberg, Tiffany M. Glassman
Items.Title: Impact of micrometeoroids on Habitable Worlds Observatory contrast stability
Items.Abstract: This paper presents ongoing investigations into the impact of micrometeoroid impacts on contrast stability for the coronagraph observations of the Habitable Worlds Observatory. We propagate properties of micrometeoroid impacts through precise coronagraph models that capture the spatial, diffractive properties of micrometeoroid-induced wavefront changes, as well as the temporal behavior of the spacecraft after impact. These calculations cover the case of micrometeoroid strikes on the telescope optics—primary or secondary. In the first case, the wavefront perturbation associated with the hypothetical impact will be localized on a primary segment or induce a secondary tilt, yielding a beam shear. In the second case, the observatory pointing will be perturbed.

Items.Authors: George Kosugi, Eisuke Morita, Hiroshi Yoshida, Kento Aida, Takeshi Nakazato, Kanako Sugimoto, Makoto Shizugami
Items.Title: Implementation and cost estimation of ALMA archive using cloud technology
Items.Abstract: The Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) currently archives nearly 300 TB of observational and processed data annually, totaling 2.3 PB. These data are first stored in Chile main archive and then copied to each regional archives in North America, Europe, and East Asia for permanent storage and provision to the science community. With the upcoming Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU), the data rate is expected to increase by an order of magnitude, raising concerns about escalating archive costs. Our group has evaluated commercial cloud platforms for hosting ALMA archives over several years. This presentation provides cost estimates for operating NAOJ's full archive on cloud services under current and WSU conditions, proposes a unified global architecture to ensure equitable access from each region, and assesses its operational costs. These findings provide a basis for strategic decisions regarding future ALMA archive operations.

Items.Authors: Chris Waring
Items.Title: Implementation of robust safety systems for the ESO VLT telescope instrumentation with MOONS as case study
Items.Abstract: As astronomical instruments grow in complexity, safety compliance must evolve from retrospective paperwork into a proactive engineering parameter. This paper presents a framework for navigating European safety regulations, specifically the EU Machinery Directive and ESO procedures. Using the MOONS Rotating Front End (RFE) as a case study, we embed safety systematically into the design lifecycle. The methodology bridges hazard analysis (ISO 12100) with quantitative validation (ISO 13849-1) to support a formal Declaration of Incorporation. By integrating inherently safe mechanics with drive-integrated TwinSAFE logic and redundant relays, the MOONS RFE mitigates risks. Validation confirmed the architecture achieved a Category 4 Performance Level (PL) e rating (MTTF_D: 1977 years; DC: 99.0%), safely exceeding the baseline PL c requirement. This quantitative approach provides a generalisable blueprint for safe instrument integration.

Items.Authors: Faouzi M. Boussaha, Piercarlo DP Bonifacio, Zhaohang Peng, Cyril Pannetier, Jean-Philippe Amans, Frédéric Sayède, Jie Hu, Paul Nicaise, Christine Chaumont, Josiane Firminy, Florent Reix, Elisabetta Caffau, Moustapha Dekkali, Michel Piat
Items.Title: Implementation of SPIAKID (spectro-photometric imaging for astronomy with kinetic inductance detectors) instrument
Items.Abstract: We report on the implementation of SPIAKID (Spectro-Photometric Imaging for Astronomy with Kinetic Inductance Detectors) instrument. It will be dedicated to primarily observe and study ultra faint dwarf (UFD) galaxies in the Local Group. SPIAKID will use 130 x 130 pixel TiN-based MKID arrays that we will be arranged in a mosaic of 4 arrays to cover 2x2 arcmin field of view and operating in 400-1600 nm wavelength range, cooled down in a 100mK dilution cryostat. Here, we will give an overview of the instrument design by focusing on detector, optical system and readout electronics configurations that are being implemented.

Items.Authors: Thomas J. Mozdzen, Richard M. Scott, Isaac Smith, Phil D. Mauskopf, Mickey Martini, Mereia Perera-Gonzalez
Items.Title: Improved timing jitter in stellar intensity interferometry while observing Sirius with 0.25m telescopes
Items.Abstract: We improve upon our intensity interferometry results from early 2024 of our observations of Sirius by using lower jitter firmware on our Swabian Time Tagger and a shorter fiber optics cable with a graded instead of a step index. We also present preliminary results showing the suppression of t=0 crosstalk noise in the Timetagger by using two Timetaggers and a Synchronizer unit, which replaces the need for coax delay cable on a single channel that is susceptible to timing variations and thus jitter. Preliminary work using a spectrometer and a linear SPAD array to decrease data collection time while maintaining a strong SNR will also be presented.

Items.Authors: Saanika Choudhary, Dmitry Savransky, Clarissa R. Do O
Items.Title: Improving the efficiency of dynamic completeness calculations for exoplanet direct imaging
Items.Abstract: Direct exoplanet imaging mission studies use dynamic completeness, the probability of detecting a planet given prior observations, to guide scheduling and estimate yield. Computing it is challenging: brute-force Monte Carlo is expensive, and common approximations often miss the true evolution of detectability. We analyze the numerical behavior of dynamic completeness, identifying cost- and accuracy-dominant steps, including repeated Kepler-equation solves and the mapping from orbital elements to observables. We further introduce a reduced-order uncertainty-propagation framework that carries orbital and photometric uncertainties through parameter distributions, enabling efficient, uncertainty-aware completeness estimates for the Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument.

Items.Authors: Chengkui Li, Shumei Jia, Juan Zhang, Yong Chen, Haisheng Zhao, Ju Guan, Xiaofan Zhao, Jingjing Xu
Items.Title: In flight energy calibration of EP-FXT
Items.Abstract: EP-FXT is a focusing soft X-ray telescope operating in the ~0.5–10 keV band, designed for sensitive follow-up imaging and spectroscopy of transient and variable sources. In orbit, we calibrate the energy–channel (EC) relation by fitting astrophysical emission lines and on-board calibration source. We construct and refine the response matrix files (RMFs). We also calibrate the grade distribution of events, quantifying the energy-dependent fractions of single- and multi-pixel grades. The calibration products ensure a stable spectral response, enabling reliable flux and spectral-parameter measurements for EP’s time-domain X-ray science.

Items.Authors: Eliad Peretz, john C. Mather, Stuart B. Shaklan, Ahmed M. Mohamed, Marc Boucher, Jean T. Landry, Christine E. Gregg
Items.Title: Inflatable starshade architectures for direct imaging of earthlike exoplanets
Items.Abstract: Inflatable starshades offer a path to achieving the large apertures required for direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets without the mass, volume, and deployment complexity of rigid architectures. We present an inflatable starshade design that integrates petal-based torus geometry, Kapton–resin laminates for post-deployment rigidization, and a simplified inflation system, enabling stowage within standard launch fairings. Recent structural and thermal analyses demonstrate that the inflatable framework can withstand lateral and vertical disturbances with acceptable safety margins, while identifying thermal gradients as the primary driver of dimensional instability. A baseline architecture is used to evaluate edge fidelity, deployment repeatability, mass drivers, and shielding strategies. We discuss requirements, risks, and the path toward sub-millimeter precision needed for 10⁻¹⁰ contrast. This work outlines the feasibility and remaining challenges of inflatable starshade
